title: Evaluating Agentic Applications End to End
summary: How to build the evaluation for your own agent: define success per task as a checkable outcome, score trajectories and tool calls, test against simulated users in resettable environments, use judges over traces where rules cannot decide, measure reliability and cost per successful task, and assemble it all into a plan that gates releases and watches production.
objectives: After this lesson you can write task specifications whose success is an objective check on the environment's final state
Score a trajectory with tool-call precision, recall and F1 plus ordering and policy constraints
Design a simulated user and a resettable sandbox, and estimate how simulator error affects measured success
Use and calibrate a judge over agent traces for criteria that rules cannot check
Combine pass^k, cost per successful task and safety metrics into a complete agent evaluation plan
prerequisites: Traces, trajectory metrics and pass^k from [/learn/agents/traces-and-evaluation](/learn/agents/traces-and-evaluation), agent benchmarks from [/learn/agents/agent-benchmarks](/learn/agents/agent-benchmarks), and judge calibration from [/learn/evaluation/eval-driven-development](/learn/evaluation/eval-driven-development).
